facts.fact: 2Africa submarine cable landed at Qua Iboe Beach, Akwa Ibom State, on 20 February 2024, via a modular cable landing station built by MainOne Solutions by Equinix; PR1 in Port Harcourt was ready December 2025, fed by 2Africa (TechCabal).

TechCabal quotes MainOne's legal director saying six or seven cables landed in Lagos, and the article says nearly all of Nigeria's seven subsea cables land in Lagos; ACE, MainOne, SAT-3 and WACS were cut by a landslide off Cote d'Ivoire in March 2024, a temporary outage.

Nigeria's international cables land at two stations: most at Lagos, and 2Africa at Qua Iboe, Akwa Ibom, the first landing outside Lagos, with PR1 Port Harcourt providing an alternate route when Lagos is disrupted (TechCabal).

Equinix/MainOne provides the 2Africa landing facilities, middle-mile fibre and carrier-neutral data centre PR1 so network operators, cloud providers and enterprises can plug into the capacity; the cable itself belongs to a consortium (TechCabal).
